title: You Need Better Attention Priors
claim: A learned prior decomposes into a key-only sink term plus a translation-equivariant relative term, which together yield the induced attention distribution.
layout: 2x2 heatmap grid, reading left-to-right then down, with + and → operators between panels
description: A 2x2 grid of heatmaps shows how a learned log-prior is built from parts. Panel (a) Sink is a red-orange map with a strong vertical stripe at the leftmost key column that fades to the right. Panel (b) Relative is a blue map with diagonal stripes, which show a translation-equivariant pattern. A plus sign sits between (a) and (b). Panel (c) Total, in the bottom left, sums the two as red and blue diagonal bands with a red left edge. A right arrow leads to panel (d) Probability, in the bottom right. Panel (d) is a causal lower-triangular map in an inferno colormap, bright at the top-left and dark at the bottom-right, with white above the diagonal. A diverging red-blue Log-Prior colorbar sits on the left and an inferno log10(Prob) colorbar on the right. A small axes inset marks query position i and key position j. The eye goes first to the colorful sink stripe and the diagonal patterns.
caption: Learned GOAT log-prior decomposition on a toy copy-mixture task. Task: train a small causal LM on synthetic sequences where each token is a mixture of copying the first token (global), copying the previous token (local), or random noise. (a) Key-only sink component Ksink(i, j) = u(j). (b) Translationequivariant relative component Krel(i, j) = κ(i −j). (c) Rowcentered total log-prior K (row shifts do not affect softmax). (d) Induced causal prior probabilities after masking to j ≤i and row-normalizing with softmax (axes shown: query position i, key position j).
abstract: We generalize the attention mechanism by viewing it through the lens of Entropic Optimal Transport, revealing that standard attention corresponds to a transport problem regularized by an implicit uniform prior. We introduce Generalized Optimal transport Attention with Trainable priors (GOAT), a new attention mechanism that replaces this naive assumption with a learnable, continuous prior. This prior maintains full compatibility with optimized kernels such as FlashAttention. GOAT also provides an EOT-based explanation of attention sinks and materializes a solution for them, avoiding the representational trade-offs of standard attention. Finally, by absorbing spatial information into the core attention computation, GOAT learns an extrapolatable prior that combines the flexibility of learned positional embeddings with the length generalization of fixed encodings.
